title: A hybrid quantum-classical neural network for learning to route
authors: Marcus Rolf Peter Ritt, Alexsandro Santos da Rosa Júnior, Marcos Vinicius Reballo, Cesar Augusto do Amaral, Fernando Augusto Caletti de Barros
abstract: This work studies hybrid quantum-classical neural networks for learning routing heuristics. Specifically, this paper asks whether small quantum neural networks can replace parameter-heavy modules inside a competitive attention-based routing model while maintaining solution quality. For the capacitated vehicle routing problem, encoder feed-forward replacement emerges as the most promising design: it reduces the number of model parameters by 56.6% while keeping the hybrid model close to the classical neural baseline at small and medium instance sizes, although the gap grows for larger instances. This work also compares to classical routing algorithms, which remain highly competitive and often superior on the fixed Euclidean test sets. Our results therefore do not indicate quantum advantage or solver dominance, but identify encoder feed-forward replacement as a viable hybrid-module compression strategy for neural combinatorial optimization.
summary: This paper investigates using hybrid quantum-classical neural networks to solve the CVRP, aiming to replace large, parameter-heavy classical modules with compact Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs). The authors successfully show that this replacement significantly reduces model size while maintaining competitive solution quality compared to classical baselines, suggesting a viable compression strategy for neural combinatorial optimization.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of learning to solve the strongly NP-hard Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) using machine learning models.
main_result: Replacing a parameter-heavy feed-forward module in a classical attention-based routing network with a small Quantum Neural Network (QNN) successfully reduces model parameters by 56.6% while maintaining solution quality close to the classical baseline for small to medium instances.
method: The authors employ a hybrid quantum-classical neural network trained via the REINFORCE algorithm to optimize routing heuristics for the CVRP.
model_or_system: The problem is modeled using an arc-based integer programming formulation for CVRP. The proposed model is a hybrid network where the classical encoder's feed-forward block is replaced by a variational QNN circuit utilizing rotations and CNOT gates.
key_observables: Objective value (route length), average relative deviation ($r_m$), and total evaluation time ($t$) when solving CVRP instances of size $n \in \{10, 20, 50, 100\}$.
important_parameters: The QNN uses a small configuration ($q=4$ qubits, $L_q=2$ layers), and performance is tested across varying instance sizes ($n$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation noted is that the performance gap between the hybrid model and the classical baseline grows for larger instances, and the comparison does not prove quantum advantage over classical heuristics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the encoder and decoder architectures of the classical model, and Figure 3 details the integration of the QNN to replace the feed-forward block.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the CVRP as the optimization problem, details the classical attention model, proposes the hybrid QNN replacement strategy in the encoder, trains and tests the model on varying instance sizes, and concludes by comparing performance against classical solvers.
why_interesting: The work demonstrates a practical application of quantum circuits to compress and accelerate components within complex machine learning models used for combinatorial optimization, which is a key area of ML-physics intersection.
